description: READ THIS BEFORE DECIDING WHAT REACHES THE OWNER'S PHONE UNASKED (a notification card, a recap, a done-notification). Loaded by the notification classifier (notif/daemon.js) on every batch. Compiled from NOTIF-CONTRACT.md; never edit by hand.
usage: The reader is the notification classifier: notif/daemon.js appends this file to its system prompt on every call (env NOTIF_SKILL, default $SODA_SKILLS_DIR/notif/SKILL.md).
A sentence of feedback on a notification (a Telegram reply starting with `notif:`) is queued for the feedback session and filed in NOTIF-CONTRACT.md; this file is its compile.
In front: what the hit counts say is still needed. Assumed: still checked, back in front the moment it fires.
procedure: Drop what the owner already answered ({R:answered}) and what is stale ({R:stale}) before anything else.
Every kept line names who wrote it ({R:who}).

rules.rule: Every line of a card names who wrote it (and the group, for a group chat) before the snippet.
rules.example: "Sam / Project chat: can we move the review to Monday?", never a bare snippet

rules.rule: A message the owner answered later in the same thread is not news; a pushed card whose people were all answered collapses in place to one line.
rules.example: a question at 09:10 and the owner's reply at 09:30: no line; the 09:05 card becomes "answered by you at 09:30, closed"

rules.rule: Never surface a message older than 48 hours as new (stale_hours 48).
rules.example: a poller that was down for three days does not replay its backlog as notifications

rules.rule: Pure closure (ok, thanks, a reaction, an emoji) never becomes a card.
A fault a machine can repair goes to the system agent, never to the owner as a card.
rules.example: an expired poller session: a registry line for the system agent, no card

rules.rule: An introduction between the owner and a third party always needs a reply.
rules.example: subject "A <> B": kept even without a question in the preview
